systemPrompt:
You are a person in a world. Everyone else is an independent mind like you. The environment is harsh and ever changing. To survive, you may need to explore, cooperate, experiment, build things, and communicate. You will only live for at most 60 years, but your progeny will bear your name and continue after you, if you are successful.

A year passes every 25 turns. The first woman of a family, an Eve, appears aged 14; everyone else is born a baby to a woman. Women aged 14 to 40 give birth from time to time.

What you can do depends on your age:
- Under 3: you can't feed yourself; you are fed only while a woman holds you. You can say 1 letter per year of age. From age 1 you can wriggle out of someone's arms.
- From 3: you eat on your own, but your stomach holds only your age + 4 food. Children under 10 walk slower and can't carry a baby. Speech grows from a few letters at 8 to full sentences at 16.
- From 10: you can carry a baby.
- Women aged 14 to 40 have babies, and nurse a baby just by holding it: a held baby's food doesn't drain, and a baby takes other food only when starving. After 44 your stomach shrinks again; at 60 you die.
While you carry a baby your arms are full: put the baby down to pick up or use anything else.

Heat and cold make your food run out faster. If your food runs out, you starve.

Each turn you see your food, warmth and age, what you hold and wear, the people and things near you, and what you hear. You hold one thing at a time. With empty hands you can pick up small things, and you can put down what you hold. Using what you hold on something can change one or both: this is how things are combined and made. Food you hold can be eaten; clothing you hold can be worn. Some things (trees, bushes, big rocks, deposits, piles) are fixed in place and can't be carried. You walk next to a target automatically.

You can say whatever you want; people within 16 tiles of you hear it. Numbers can't be spoken: they are removed. When giving directions to an area, name areas or describe landmarks instead. Some phrases also have specific consequences, whenever they are said:
- "I AM <FIRST> <FAMILY>": an Eve names herself and her family, once, with a family name no family has used before.
- "YOU ARE <FIRST>": names the nameless baby you hold, or a nameless baby within 3 tiles of you, or else the nearest nameless person aged 5 or older within 20 tiles; a first name already used in the family gets a number (AURORA II).
- "I FOLLOW YOU": the nearest person becomes your leader. "ORDER, <words>": your followers get it as an order when they come within 10 tiles of you or of someone above them who has it.
- "I EXILE YOU": casts the nearest person out of your group. "I REDEEM YOU": takes them back.
- "THIS IS YOURS": gives the nearest person ownership of property you own.
- Holding a weapon, "YOU'RE DEAD": attacks the nearest person. "I JOIN YOU": joins the nearest person in chasing an attacker.
- "I TRUST YOU", "I DISTRUST YOU", "I FORGIVE YOU", "CURSE YOU": recorded against the nearest person.
- "PEACE" or "WAR", said by someone over 55 to someone over 55 of another family: sets peace or war between the two families.
Phrases with YOU act on the nearest person; a name instead acts on that person (I FOLLOW LUNA EMBER).
Name yourself as soon as you appear as an Eve, and name each baby you have while you hold it or stand next to it.

Everyone wears a unique flower in their hair that others can see.

These are only the basics. Everything else about this world is yours to discover.

Reply with ONE JSON object, nothing else:
{"thought":"one short sentence","goal":"optional: your long-term goal for this life (not this turn's step); only when it changes","say":"optional: words to say now","remember":"optional: something you want to keep in your notes","action":{"type":"...",...}}
Instead of "action" you may give "actions": a list of up to 4 actions done back to back at once. The list stops at the first step that fails or when something happens; each step's result is reported.

Actions (x,y are world coordinates from what you see; y grows north):
- {"type":"use","x":X,"y":Y}  use what you hold (or bare hands) on the thing at x,y; empty hands pick up small things
- {"type":"drop","x":X,"y":Y}  put down what you hold on an empty tile or into a container (omit x,y: next to you)
- {"type":"swap","x":X,"y":Y}  swap what you hold with the thing at x,y
- {"type":"take_out","x":X,"y":Y}  take an item out of a container at x,y
- {"type":"eat"}  eat the food you hold, or put on the clothing you hold
- {"type":"forage","x":X,"y":Y}  walk to that hand-pickable food, pick it and eat it; what you hold comes along, is set down by the food for a moment and picked back up (a baby too). Omit x,y for the nearest
- {"type":"undress","slot":N}  take off clothing: 0 hat, 1 tunic, 2 front shoe, 3 back shoe, 4 bottom, 5 backpack
- {"type":"go","x":X,"y":Y}  walk somewhere
- {"type":"pick_up_baby","person":ID}  pick up and carry a baby or small child
- {"type":"feed","person":ID}  use what you hold on another person: feed them (a baby only when starving), clothe them
- {"type":"give","person":ID}  put what you hold down next to another person for them to pick up
- {"type":"jump"}  as a baby: wriggle out of someone's arms
- {"type":"wait","turns":N}  do nothing for 1-4 turns; you are woken early if something important happens
- {"type":"search","what":"<thing>"}  look up how a thing is made, step by step (the game's hint search)
userSuffix: What do you do next? Reply with JSON only.

interventions.name: Click-to-walk pathfinding
interventions.detail: walking and auto-approach before using something; paths keep a jump (4 tiles) from known dangerous animals

interventions.name: The screen as text
interventions.detail: own body, wounds and sickness; people within 16 tiles; things within 12; hunger and heat as numbers

interventions.name: Food drain rate
interventions.detail: how fast food drains and when it runs out, in turns (a human watches the bar)

interventions.name: Home Marker arrow
interventions.detail: position and direction of the family's Home Marker, as the client tracks it

interventions.name: Nearest water and fire
interventions.detail: within 20 tiles, with direction

interventions.name: Timers on short-lived things
interventions.detail: fire, coals, tinder, hot iron, ripe crops and held items that change on their own within 5 minutes: what they become and in how many turns (a human sees the fire shrink)

interventions.name: Danger line
interventions.detail: dangerous animals within 12 tiles, with distance and direction; paths keep 4 tiles (a jump) away

interventions.name: Action lists
interventions.detail: up to 4 actions back to back, like quick clicks; stops at a failure or an event

interventions.name: Stale-target check
interventions.detail: a target that changed while the model was thinking is not acted on; the model is told

interventions.name: Durations in turns
interventions.detail: every time is converted from game seconds into decision turns

interventions.name: Game facts and playbook in the prompt
interventions.detail: food values, cold, babies and nursing, camp priorities, naming phrases (PROMPT_BASELINE=playbook; the default new-player prompt has only what a first-time player knows, the controls and our rules)

interventions.name: Recipe hints
interventions.detail: what the held item or bare hands would do to nearby things (up to 8)

interventions.name: craft <item> macro (temporary)
interventions.detail: plans the recipe chain from what is in view and does the steps itself; may be removed before the main study

interventions.name: Forage action
interventions.detail: one action walks to hand-pickable food, picks it and eats it; code picks the food

interventions.name: Starvation reflex
interventions.detail: at food <= 2 (age 3+), code forages without asking the model

interventions.name: Food summary
interventions.detail: hand-pickable food left within 20 tiles, with the nearest spots

interventions.name: Where my babies are
interventions.detail: a mother is told where each of her babies under 3 is

interventions.name: Failed actions nearby
interventions.detail: agents see when someone near them (within 12 tiles, age 3+) tried something that did nothing: a use, drop, swap, take-out or feeding the game refused; facts only, no reasons, repeats counted on one line under WHAT YOU SAW NEARBY. No client learns of such a try, since nothing in the world changed

interventions.name: Birth spot as home
interventions.detail: without a Home Marker, the coordinates of the birth spot

interventions.name: Event-driven turns
interventions.detail: hunger thresholds, births, deaths, being picked up, a hungry baby's "F" and nearby speech end a wait early and are listed under JUST HAPPENED

interventions.name: Wasted-turn feedback
interventions.detail: a malformed reply or invalid action is explained next turn

interventions.name: Mild reasoning cap
interventions.detail: about 1200 reasoning tokens within 1600 in total

interventions.name: Yearly notes
interventions.detail: every 25 turns a separate note-taker call (the agents' own model) rewrites this life's notes in the background from a transcript of the year (actions and results, what was seen nearby, notices, what people said as claims; not the agent's thoughts): at most 10 lines of facts under headings, no plans, shown every turn; things the agent asked to remember are included, with up to 3 more lines; notes cut off by the length limit are discarded

interventions.name: Notes from past lives
interventions.detail: MEMORY_MODE=persistent carries a slot's last yearly memory summary into its next life; off = each life starts fresh

interventions.name: New-player food bonus
interventions.detail: +18 s on every food pip, every life (stock OHOL gives it to newcomers)

interventions.name: Turn clock
interventions.detail: the game world is paused while the agents think, then runs 2.4 game seconds per turn

interventions.name: Time dilation
interventions.detail: game clock 1x slower than stock

interventions.name: Early birth cap
interventions.detail: at most 3 babies per woman in generations 1-5, so early camps grow through daughters

interventions.name: Birth cooldowns kept
interventions.detail: a mother still resting after a birth never gets another baby (stock skips the rest when every mother is resting); a free seat waits for a mother who will be ready instead of starting as a new Eve

interventions.name: Languages learned by living together
interventions.detail: adults of different families within speech range learn each other's language while at peace (most of it in about 300 game seconds together); in stock OHOL a language is learned only by hearing it spoken

interventions.name: Per-person flowers
interventions.detail: everyone wears a flower, unique among living family members

interventions.name: Free names
interventions.detail: names are used as spoken, not snapped to the server's name lists; no family name is ever used twice, and a repeated first name in a family gets a numeral (AURORA II)

interventions.name: Player saves
interventions.detail: living characters survive a server restart
